note: What each workshop app's planner receives. `problem` is what the participant types (short, in their words); `facilitator_brief` is the minimal steering, shown to participants as "Facilitator's brief". Written 2 Nov 2026.

s7-1-dashboard.title: Your country's recommendations dashboard
s7-1-dashboard.problem: I need to see what UN human rights mechanisms have told my country, and find the exact paragraphs fast.
s7-1-dashboard.facilitator_brief: A dashboard on the participant's country's file from the Universal Human Rights Index. It should be trustworthy enough for a diplomat preparing a meeting: every number explained, every paragraph one click from its UN document, and a way to check the UN's own labels on a random sample.

s7-4-extract.title: Paragraphs out of a PDF
s7-4-extract.problem: Our office copies paragraphs out of UN PDFs by hand. Can a tool split a General Comment into its numbered paragraphs, and show me where it got things wrong?
s7-4-extract.facilitator_brief: The file is the raw text of CESCR General comment No. 27 as a PDF converter produced it, page by page, with a reference (paragraph and footnote counts, first words of each paragraph). The tool must check itself against the reference and make every repair it makes visible.

s8-1-verbatim.title: Verbatim finder for General Comments
s8-1-verbatim.problem: When I draft a submission I need the exact words of a General Comment and a correct citation. Help me find them.
s8-1-verbatim.facilitator_brief: A search tool over every General Comment paragraph of the treaty bodies: it retrieves, it never generates. Boolean search and exact phrases, citations ready to paste, and a way to collect quotations for a draft.

s8-5-wiki.title: A research wiki on neurotechnology and justice
s8-5-wiki.problem: Our team keeps losing track of what each report says about neurotechnology in the justice system. Build us a research wiki we can trust and keep up to date.
s8-5-wiki.facilitator_brief: The wiki is already compiled from nine sources (WORKSHOP_DATA.wiki), following Karpathy's LLM-wiki pattern as kept in a book project: source, concept, entity and question pages, verified pins that open the PDF page, registers and contested claims. The app is the team's workspace for it: read and navigate, Ask the wiki and file good answers back, Ingest the waiting source A/HRC/57/61 with a human approving each change, and Lint. The model drafts; the code verifies every quotation.
